annotations.text: The drawer has two homes and the landing is only one of them. In the stands the landing page is on screen, so its column can absorb anything. In the cockpit there is no landing, and a pilot still needs volume, side, and a way to leave the seat. Whatever replaces the drawer has to answer the corner MENU key, or the drawer survives for flight and we have two systems instead of one.
B, at home: the corner MENU key becomes a settings key, icon only, and opens the panel in place over the stars. Same panel everywhere, drawer deleted. This is the direction I would take.

B, flying: the same key mid-match. Leave and Side ride at the head of the panel, because they only mean anything in a seat. This board is what the whole proposal stands on: if this works, nothing needs the drawer.

A: a fourth SETTINGS stop in the landing column, opening upward from its row. Honest about where settings live, but it reads oddly in the who-where-what sentence the column speaks, and it answers only the stands. The cockpit still needs a key, and once that key exists it may as well open the same panel, which is B.

C: settings folded under the account list, drawn to be ruled out. It buries sound and controls behind an identity chooser they have nothing to do with, trims rows to fit, and still says nothing about flight.
